what: The lobby offers three missions in order: Weather satellite (Start here), Lunar ice lander (Next step), Mars orbiter + lander (Harder). The new mission sends one lander to the Moon: launch to low orbit, transfer to the Moon (no window, ~5 days), brake into lunar orbit, land, drill for ice (3 goals, budget 260 M, launch day 300, deadline day 455). The starting design cannot lift off (one 2,000 kN engine under 305 t, lift ratio 0.67) and the one-click tank fix does not cure that, so the Planner must choose: two booster engines (fast to buy, two chances to fail) or one 4,500 kN engine (safer, more margin, eight months from Tallis or four months through a Comms deal with Feldwerk). Science has two needs from the first second (drill-and-oven lab 4.5 vs 3.2, descent engine Isp 312 vs 310). Communications has its own Moon content: a new character (Dr. Amara Kessler, crewed landing-site team), six timeline messages, eight player-triggered, three state-triggered and twelve pool messages, six projects (two of them reach into other stations' main decisions: the Feldwerk booster offer and the Northgate regolith lab that raises the lab limit), four in-flight events. The planner briefing lists 'New in this mission' in four beginner sentences. A Moon transfer now follows a moved launch date instead of breaking the plan.

verified: npx tsc --noEmit clean; npx vite build --outDir ../playtest/runs/m-build passes. Five spec checks in the running planner (port 4720): (1) starting design lift ratio 0.67, launch mass 305.05 t (scratch evaluation with the game's evaluate()); the screen says 'Too weak to lift off (lift ratio 0.67, needs above 1). Add engines to the first stage.' With the 2.5-t legs the start is also 0.12 km/s short at the landing, so the planner offers 'Bigger descent stage tank' (0.70 -> 0.88 t); after it the lift-off error stays. (2) Booster x2: 0.16 km/s short after that first fix (0.284 km/s from the untouched start), the fix sizes the lander tank to 1.18 t. (3) Twin booster with the bought 1.6 t tank and 2.5 t legs: margin +0.15 km/s (154 m/s); single KL-4500 with bought parts: +0.37 km/s (371 m/s). (4) Transfer to Moon uses 3.13 km/s, 5 d (4.98 d in the model), Enter Moon orbit 0.82 km/s at 100 km. (5) Science 'The mission needs' shows exactly: Surface lab performance >= 4.5 (Lab automation 14 M, 3 mo, finish by 28 Apr) and Storable hypergolic engine Isp >= 312 s (Hypergolic injector tuning 8 M, 1.8 mo, finish by 29 Jul). Flight 1, twin booster (session m-check, harness 0.5x): 2x KL-2000 from Swift (76.4 M), all parts by suggestion except a Commons upper engine; the lander tank arrived as Flask PT-1.6, margin +0.15 km/s, no legs error; Lab automation failed once, retry plus Comms' vacuum chamber, joint lab and test technicians finished it 21 Jul; lab from Meridian arrived 4 Feb 2031; 'Next: move launch' moved the launch to 5 Feb 2031 (that is where the transfer broke before the logic.ts change); booster engines tested (95.1 -> 97.5 %); result 3/3 goals, launch day 400, mission end 20 Mar 2031, spend 259.3 M of 240 M (Treasury took 20 M while I was on another station). Flight 2, one big engine (session m-check4, 2x with the calendar paused while I clicked): Science started both needs on day 4, Comms ran Supplier roundtable (industry 55) then 'Booster engine from Feldwerk' (offer on day ~66); Procurement signed Feldwerk's 4,500 kN engine (55 M, 4 months, delivered 9 Aug); lab research succeeded (7 Apr), lab ordered day 99 from Meridian; a pool message I missed slipped every delivery a month, Comms' expediting bonus moved the lab back to 10 Oct, the descent engine stayed late (8 Nov), the Planner pressed 'Next: move launch to 9 Nov 2030' and the transfer moved with it (0 errors); upper engine and antenna tested; result 3/3 goals, launch day 312, mission end 13 Dec 2030, spend 210.6 M of 240 M. An earlier attempt of flight 2 (m-check3) found that the Feldwerk offer without a mass weighed the generic 0.4 t engine estimate (margin +0.74 km/s instead of +0.37); fixed by giving it the catalogue mass 6.95 t and verified in m-check4. Weather (manual lobby, three cards in order on the picker) and Mars (auto lobby) start and look as before: weather 9 parts, 350 M, launch 30 Jun, weather Comms projects, no 'New in this mission'; Mars 16 parts, 900 M, launch 19 Aug, Mars Comms with licences. All sessions stopped; no process of this checkout left running.
notVerified: Four players at once (all play was one player switching stations). Normal speed end to end: flight 1 ran at half speed, flight 2 at double speed with pauses; minutes at normal speed are computed from game days (30.44 days = 1 minute). The touchdown masses (1.13 t / 1.21 t) are not shown on screen; the legs check passed (no legs error). The lean single-engine variant (0.7 t tank, 1 t legs) no longer exists by design. The Northgate regolith lab route (limit 5) was offered but not completed in a run. The Comms follow-up 'You promised me a date' expired unseen in flight 1 (its -20 Government landed). A failed Moon flight and the restart path. The 'Still on the ground' answer that re-promises a date was answered but the later break of that promise was not reached.
risk: Balance: the budget is tight on purpose (260 M; parts 200-212 M with the suggestions, research 22 M), and a research retry plus one ignored budget message can push the twin design over budget (flight 1 ended at 259 M of 240 M). Lab automation is 85 %; it failed in 2 of 3 first attempts I played, which slips the launch to about day 400 (13 min) - still inside the deadline 455. The lab window is narrow: Science must start the lab research by about day 26 (52 s) or the standard lab delivery arrives after day 300, so many first-time teams will move the launch a little. The suggestion ranks a Comms partner offer below a catalogue part of the same mass but higher reliability, so the Feldwerk engine is only bought when Procurement picks it (it is shown as 'Partner offer · 55 M' on the need and 'Cheapest on time' in the order dialog). If the light descent engine is late, the switch list offers the heavier Vesta HT-35; with the twin booster that leaves -2 m/s, and the tank fix then asks for a 4 t tank (Flask PT-4, +0.20 km/s, legs still fine), so it is one more fix and rebuy, not a dead end. logic.ts change: any transfer from the launch body to one of its moons now keeps its offset to the launch when the launch moves; in the Mars mission this only touches a player-made Earth-to-Moon transfer (never part of a normal Mars plan). The harness picks a lobby card by any text it contains: the Moon card must not name the other missions (comment added).
coreRequests: core/mission.ts was edited (registration only: import MOON_LANDER, MISSIONS = [WEATHER_GEO, MOON_LANDER, MARS_ORBITER_LANDER]) as this package's prompt allowed.
foreignRequests: planner/model/types.ts: optional `ideas?: string[]` on MissionDef, read only by Briefing.tsx. Reason: the spec's 'New in this mission' sentences need a per-mission place; weather and Mars leave it undefined and show nothing new.

planner/logic.ts setLaunch(): transfers to a moon of the launch body shift with the launch (m.departDay += next - prev). Reason: without it, every launch move in the Moon mission (frequent: late lab, failed research, late deliveries) left 'Departure before arrival in orbit' on the transfer, and the planner's own 'Next: move launch' button led straight into that error. Transfers to planets (Mars windows) are untouched.

Optional, not done: the planner's NextStep route hint stops after 'Enter orbit' (routeHint returns null for a land goal at a body already orbited); a 'Next: + Next step at Moon -> Land on Moon' hint would help first-time Planners. The engine-count control is behind 'Advanced'; the briefing sentence points there.
specChanges: Landing legs start at 2.5 t (Strider LG-2.5) instead of 1 t. Every tank the fix proposes (0.79-1.59 t) is bought as the full 1.6 t Flask; with 1-t legs that broke the landing after the contracts were signed (touchdown 1.12 t). With 2.5-t legs a bought tank only adds margin. Consequences: the starting design is also 0.12 km/s short at the landing (the fix button appears, cures the fuel, not the lift-off); booster x2 is 0.28 km/s short and the fix proposes 1.18 t instead of 0.86 t; the lean single-engine variant (0.7 t tank, 1 t legs, 98 m/s) is gone; both workable designs end at the spec's numbers (154 m/s and 371 m/s).

Comms content follows the current format (commit 8afd318): no missionConstraint or service effects. Kessler's 'promise' answer sets the launch-date promise flag (called in by 'You promised me a date'); 'Still on the ground' re-promises the current date instead of the untraceable 'no slack' text and says 'meant to fly in October' instead of 'your launch date has passed' (the date may have moved). Left out like the weather set: the four licences, the nuclear hearing, the ion export review and the nuclear-research hold (they block or open techs this lander never needs; Science shows those techs as 'Not in this mission'). Added the weather set's real-effect projects (Supplier roundtable, Northgate test technicians) and the vacuum-chamber message (its effect is real now: research and test pace).
Partner offers carry catalogue masses: Feldwerk's 4,500 kN engine 6.95 t (spec value; without it the game uses a 0.4 t estimate), Feldwerk's surplus upper-stage engine 0.566 t.

Audit message: 'a launch still ahead' instead of 'a lander still to buy' (with the single engine it fires after everything is bought). Budget amounts in pool messages scaled to the 260 M budget (claw-back 10/20 M, strike 1 month, infrastructure 20/12 M).
Briefing paragraph kept short; the four idea sentences carry leaving Earth, braking into orbit, landing without air (with legs) and one engine or two (pointing at Rocket -> Advanced and Push).
